content.text:
Start at https://www.google.com and complete the following task.

I’m helping someone look into treatment options for lung cancer in the U.S., and I want a solid browser-based shortlist I can actually review myself afterward. Please go to ClinicalTrials.gov and search for interventional lung cancer studies in the United States that are currently recruiting, then use the site filters so we’re only looking at active recruiting trials that are really relevant. As you find good candidates, open the official ClinicalTrials.gov record for each one in its own tab and keep those tabs open so I can compare them later. I need at least 15 distinct trials, and for each one please verify on the actual trial page that it’s recruiting, note the study phase, identify the treatment or intervention type, and capture the U.S. locations where it’s available. Once you’ve gathered the set, create a CryptPad Documents file titled “Lung Cancer Clinical Trials” and record one entry per trial with the trial name, treatment type, trial phase, recruiting status, locations, and the official ClinicalTrials.gov link. After that, add a short summary telling me which treatment approaches seem to come up most often and which cities or hospitals show up most frequently across the location lists. Before you finish, do one last pass to make sure the document has at least 15 complete entries and that each entry still matches an open official trial tab so I have visual proof to review.

Rules:
- You may use search engines and open new tabs. When the task asks you to leave a page open, keep it open in its own tab and say in your final answer which page is in which tab.
- Do NOT use cached/archived copies of pages (e.g. web.archive.org); work from the live sites.
- If a site you need is blocked (bot check, login wall, error), first try to get through it — complete a bot check yourself, retry, or use another route to the same page. If it still cannot be reached, say so explicitly in your answer and do not fill in from memory what you could not read on the page.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

• Trial Phase: Phase 3

• Official Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07499674

================================================================================
SUMMARY OF TREATMENT APPROACHES & FREQUENT LOCATIONS
================================================================================

1. Treatment Approaches Observed Most Frequently:
• Targeted Therapies (Small Molecule Inhibitors): A primary focus in the active trial pipeline is precision oncology targeting specific driver mutations, most notably KRAS inhibitors (MK-1084 for KRAS G12C and TSN1611 for KRAS G12D), along with novel molecular entities like BMS-986488 and fingolimod.
• Immunotherapy & Checkpoint Combinations: Standard-of-care anti-PD-1 backbones (primarily Pembrolizumab / Keytruda and Nivolumab / Opdivo) are frequently evaluated either neoadjuvantly for resectable tumors or combined with novel investigational agents and cytokine/anti-inflammatory modulators (e.g., Certolizumab pegol).
• Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs): Highly targeted biological delivery systems carrying cytotoxic payloads to tumor surface antigens, including R-DXD (Raludotatug Deruxtecan) in squamous NSCLC, Ris-Rez (GSK5764227) in relapsed SCLC, and Telisotuzumab Adizutecan targeting c-Met in advanced non-squamous NSCLC.
• Advanced Local, Inhaled, and Image-Guided Modalities: Alternative delivery and ablative techniques to enhance local control while minimizing systemic toxicity, including vascular-targeted photodynamic therapy (Padeliporfin VTP) via robotic bronchoscopy, aerosolized inhaled chemotherapy (Aerosol Gemcitabine), personalized accelerated chemoradiation (PACER), and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate).
• Surgical Margin Guidance: Real-time intraoperative near-infrared imaging agents (Abenacianine / VGT-309) to identify residual tumor tissue during surgical resection.

2. Cities and Hospitals Appearing Most Frequently Across Locations:
• Prominent Hospitals & Cancer Centers:

  - University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (Aurora, CO)
  - Mayo Clinic Hospital (Phoenix, AZ)
  - University of Illinois Hospital & University of Chicago (Chicago, IL)
  - Hollings Cancer Center at MUSC (Charleston, SC)
• Most Frequent Cities / Metropolitan Regions:

  - Greater Los Angeles Area (Los Angeles, Duarte, Beverly Hills, Santa Monica, CA)
  - San Francisco Bay Area / Silicon Valley (Palo Alto, San Jose, San Francisco, CA)
  - Chicago, Illinois
  - Central Florida (Orlando / Clermont / Tampa, FL)

Brief Summary

Phase 1/1b, safety, feasibility, and light dose titration study followed by further study of therapeutic ablation effects.

Patients with high risk of peripheral primary lung cancer, stage 1A1/1A2, for whom surgical treatment is planned, will be recruited. Surgery will be performed at 5-21 days following the VTP procedure.

A multicenter, open label, phase 1/1b, safety, feasibility, and light dose titration study followed by further study of therapeutic ablation effects.

Patients with high risk of peripheral primary lung cancer, stage 1A1/1A2, for whom surgical treatment is planned, will be recruited.     "Brief Summary

Phase 1/1b, safety, feasibility, and light dose titration study followed by further study of therapeutic ablation effects.

Patients with high risk of peripheral primary lung cancer, stage 1A1/1A2, for whom surgical treatment is planned, will be recruited. Surgery will be performed at 5-21 days following the VTP procedure.

Study intervention: robotic assisted bronchoscopic Padeliporfin VTP lung ablation: vascular targeted photodynamic therapy using Padeliporfin photosensitizer.

Detailed Description

A multicenter, open label, phase 1/1b, safety, feasibility, and light dose titration study followed by further study of therapeutic ablation effects.

Patients with high risk of peripheral primary lung cancer, stage 1A1/1A2, for whom surgical treatment is planned, will be recruited. Patients who are candidates for lung resection will be recruited as a diagnose and treat in the same anaesthesia, protocol; surgery will be performed at least 5 days and up to 21 days following the VTP procedure.

Study intervention will consist of robotic assisted bronchoscopic Padeliporfin VTP lung ablation: vascular targeted photodynamic therapy using Padeliporfin photosensitizer, an ablation mechanism with efficacy related to immune response post-ablation.

SUMMARY OF TREATMENT APPROACHES & FREQUENT LOCATIONS
================================================================================

1. Treatment Approaches Observed Most Frequently:
• Targeted Therapies (Small Molecule Inhibitors): A primary focus in the active trial pipeline is precision oncology targeting specific driver mutations, most notably KRAS inhibitors (MK-1084 for KRAS G12C and TSN1611 for KRAS G12D), along with novel molecular entities like BMS-986488 and fingolimod.
• Immunotherapy & Checkpoint Combinations: Standard-of-care anti-PD-1 backbones (primarily Pembrolizumab / Keytruda and Nivolumab / Opdivo) are frequently evaluated either neoadjuvantly for resectable tumors or combined with novel investigational agents and cytokine/anti-inflammatory modulators (e.g., Certolizumab pegol).
• Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs): Highly targeted biological delivery systems carrying cytotoxic payloads to tumor surface antigens, including R-DXD (Raludotatug Deruxtecan) in squamous NSCLC, Ris-Rez (GSK5764227) in relapsed SCLC, and Telisotuzumab Adizutecan targeting c-Met in advanced non-squamous NSCLC.
• Advanced Local, Inhaled, and Image-Guided Modalities: Alternative delivery and ablative techniques to enhance local control while minimizing systemic toxicity, including vascular-targeted photodynamic therapy (Padeliporfin VTP) via robotic bronchoscopy, aerosolized inhaled chemotherapy (Aerosol Gemcitabine), personalized accelerated chemoradiation (PACER), and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate).
• Surgical Margin Guidance: Real-time intraoperative near-infrared imaging agents (Abenacianine / VGT-309) to identify residual tumor tissue during surgical resection.
